heard: An invisible rogue black hole is wandering completely alone through our galaxy. In the year 2011, ground-based surveys detected a sudden spike in the brightness of a background star. This distant star is located approximately 20,000 light years away from Earth. Astronomers realized the event occurred when an unseen object bent and magnified the star's light. Using the Hubble Space Telescope, scientists spent six years measuring tiny deflections in the star's position. By verifying the lensing object emitted no light, they confirmed it was a black hole weighing about 7.1 times the mass of our sun. Located about 5,000 light years away, this phantom is hurtling through space at an estimated speed of 45 to 51 kilometers per second. An invisible rogue black hole is wandering completely alone through our galaxy.
